passage:
I'm Mahima, and I've watched Ojas say yes for years: the neighbour's shifting, the office collection, everyone's cousin's admission forms. Lately he seems different. On Sunday afternoons he doesn't answer his phone, and he told us why: "That's my nap time." A few weeks ago he handed the building's water-tank rota to three others, saying, "I'll take it one week in four."
When his colleague asked him to cover a Saturday shift, I heard him say, "I can't do this week, but I can do next month." There was no long apology.
I can't tell how it feels for him inside. He looked a bit nervous when he said no. But he also looked rested, and the people who depend on him are still getting his help.

qa.q: How often did Ojas say he would take the water-tank rota after handing it over?
qa.a: He said he would take it one week in four.

qa.q: How might Ojas feel when he says no?
qa.a: Ojas looked nervous when he refused, but also rested afterwards, so he may feel both uneasy and relieved.

qa.q: What made Ojas's no to the Saturday shift work well?
qa.a: He named what he could not do and offered a later date, without a long apology. That kept his kindness dependable.

qa.q: What is Mahima feeling as she watches Ojas set limits?
qa.a: Mahima seems curious and quietly admiring, though unsure what Ojas feels inside.

grounding: An observer sees a heavy giver schedule rest, share the load and say a clear no to some requests, keeping his kindness sustainable.

passage:
Monday. Kalyani sat on the stairs with her tuition notebooks, her eyes half closed. "I've had five kids' parents call me since Saturday," she told Zainab, who lived upstairs. "I said yes to all of them."
Wednesday. She wrote on the whiteboard in her hallway: "Sundays: closed." Then she called Zainab. "Would you share the neighbourhood tiffin rota? Just Tuesdays and Fridays?" Zainab said she would.
Saturday. A mother asked whether Kalyani could add an extra batch on Sunday. "I can't on Sundays," Kalyani said. "But I could fit it on Thursday." The mother agreed. Kalyani closed the door and let out a long breath. She slept in until eight the next morning.

qa.q: Which days did Kalyani ask Zainab to help with the tiffin rota?
qa.a: She asked Zainab to take Tuesdays and Fridays.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling on Monday as she sat on the stairs?
qa.a: Kalyani felt exhausted and overloaded, saying she had said yes to all five parents.

qa.q: What small steps did Kalyani take over the week to keep her kindness sustainable?
qa.a: She marked Sundays closed, asked Zainab to share the tiffin rota and offered a Thursday slot in place of Sunday.

qa.q: How might Zainab have felt when asked to take Tuesdays and Fridays?
qa.a: Zainab said yes, which suggests being willing and perhaps glad to be trusted. Sharing the load meant the neighbours' tiffins would still arrive.

grounding: A person who gives a lot schedules rest, shares the load and says a clear no to some requests over several days.
